lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: representing constraints by equations, inequalities, and systems
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: representing constraints by equations, inequalities, and systems

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: A tank holds 50 L and fills at 8 L/min. When does it hold 130 L?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A model gives the number of buses needed as 4.3. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Report 4.3, because the model is exact.
The model must be wrong, because the answer is not a whole number.
Round up to 5; a fractional bus is not viable and rounding down leaves people behind.
Round down to 4, because 4.3 is closer to 4.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $275 call-out fee plus $7 per hour. A job cost $366 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
The formula A = -2bh − 7 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Item A costs $6 each and item B costs $26 each. You may spend at most $170 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 240 litres and is filling at 13 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 500 litres?
A budget model allows 12.7 units of a product sold individually. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Round down to 12; buying a partial unit is not possible and 13 would exceed the budget.
Round up to 13, because 12.7 is closer to 13.
Split the order so the fractional unit is shared.
Report 12.7, because the constraint is satisfied.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $225 call-out fee plus $12 per hour. A job cost $297 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
